idiom_name: class Users(tag: Tag) extends Table[User](tag, "users") + TableQuery
implementation_notes: Scala default: the mapping is a Table subclass whose column vals and `def *` projection describe the row, with TableQuery as the table handle, while the domain type is an ordinary immutable case class. Slick composes queries over the table type and only instantiates rows on .result, so there is no instrumentation, no lazy loading and no object graph to navigate - the entity stays dumb and the table class is the metadata. Doobie's Read/Write instances are the functional alternative when SQL is written explicitly.
pitfalls: The `def *` projection must match the case class arity and order; equal types hide a swapped pair and the mapping silently exchanges columns.
Actions are lazy: mapping errors appear when the DBIO runs, not when the query is built.
Mapping every row into a full entity discards Slick's partial-column advantage; use tuples/projections on hot paths.

variants.name: Doobie Read/Write typeclass mapping
variants.idiom_name: Read[User] / Write[User] instances beside the queries
variants.implementation_notes: Functional variant: the entity is a case class and the mapping lives in Read/Write typeclass instances (derived or hand-written) next to the sql-interpolated queries, so nothing is attached to the entity and no session/proxy machinery exists. Choose it when SQL stays explicit and referential transparency matters more than an ORM's conveniences.
pitfalls: Derivation follows the SELECT column order; reordering columns silently maps the wrong values.
There is no unit of work: updates are explicit, so a forgotten Write/run leaves the database untouched.
